neighbours.label: an interviewer's question or remark addressed to the interviewee as 'you' in a Q&A transcript; the same content told about the interviewee in third person stays quiet
fire: Q: Last season you went from the bench to team captain. What changed?
Interviewer: When you started the band, did you expect this kind of success?
Rolling Stone: You have toured nonstop for three years. Are you tired?
Tell us a bit about how you first got into pottery.

Q&A
Q: Your new novel is set in Lagos. Why there?
Host: So you spent a year living in the Arctic. What was that like?
BBC: You've said before that music saved your life. Can you explain?
Q: How did you decide which recipes to include in the book?
quiet: Last season he went from the bench to team captain, and the fans noticed.
When she started the band, she did not expect this kind of success.
The singer has toured nonstop for three years and looks tired.
The article explains how the artist first got into pottery.
Her new novel is set in Lagos, where she grew up.
The explorer spent a year living in the Arctic and wrote about it.
The musician once said that music saved his life.
The chef explained how she chose the recipes for the book.

notes: Card: ' you'/' have'/' about' in interview turns ('HitFix: You have such...', 'Tell us a little about'). Probe: 'HitFix: You have' 0.962, 'Interviewer: ... you have gone' 0.784, 'Tell us a little about' 0.637, 'Q: When you are writing' 0.429; third-person versions 0.064 and 0.108; 'You have to preheat' 0.125; reported 'that you were coming' 0.400, so second-person address outside interviews also fires and no near miss uses 'you'.
